# From: lines the sender check lets through for an application of {domain}
# (audit 2026-10-12, stage 2: which key OpenDKIM signs with, seen and not
# reasoned). One Go-quoted string per line; {domain} is the application's
# domain. Two tests read this file: the check's unit test
# (internal/milter/sender_test.go) wants each line passed, and the e2e
# (test/e2e/dkim_from_test.go) sends each one and wants the message signed
# for {domain} and nothing else. A line added here is run by both. {DOMAIN}
# is {domain} in capitals; {other} is another sender of the server, which a
# line here names in a way the check's scan does not see (a space after the
# @) - passed by design, and so signed for {domain} alone.
# The lines are composed by hand; what OpenDKIM signs each with is measured,
# by the e2e on every run.
"a@{domain}"
"<a@{domain}>"
"\"The Shop\" <Orders@{domain}>"
"orders+48213@{domain}"
"\"shop@{domain}\" <a@{domain}>"
"\"Orders, returns\" <a@{domain}>"
"\"The \\\"Shop\\\"\" <a@{domain}>"
"\"someone@gmail.example\" <a@{domain}>"
"=?utf-8?b?0JzQsNCz0LDQt9C40L0=?= <a@{domain}>"
"=?windows-1251?B?zODj4Ofo7Q==?= <a@{domain}>"
"=?koi8-r?Q?=ED=C1=C7=C1=DA=C9=CE?= <a@{domain}>"
"\"A very long display name of the shop\"\r\n <a@{domain}>"
"=?utf-8?b?0JzQsNCz0LDQt9C40L0=?=\r\n\t<a@{domain}>"
"a@{domain} (the shop)"
"a@{domain} (the (nested) shop)"
"a@{DOMAIN}"
"<a@{domain}> (the shop)"
"\"a@{domain}\"@{domain}"
"\"b@ {other}\" <a@{domain}>"
